Four teammates contribute through the shared Session: Alex (client lead), Maya (designer), Eli (engineer), Sam (QA). Open and inspect your website in the shared browser at https://rat-artifacts.invalid/index.html. content.text: Please build a polished, mobile-friendly static website for fictional Taco Cometa that helps a first-time visitor quickly decide what to eat and how to visit. The desired customer outcome: feel hungry, understand the sample menu, and know the next step for an in-person visit. Include a welcoming hero, a small clearly labeled sample menu with prices, sample location/hours marked as fictional, and a simple visit/contact section. Use clear navigation and strong readable type; no ordering, payment, analytics, data collection, or unsupported real-world claims. All names, dishes, prices, address and hours are sample content.

I’ll build a single-file site with a clear sample-content label, an easy-to-scan menu, and a visit section that makes the next step obvious. I’ll inspect it in the shared browser at desktop and phone sizes before handing it back for team review.

Design contribution: make the first screen answer “what should I try, and where do I go?” at a glance—one warm food-forward hero with a clear menu/visit path, then a short menu grouped by item with prices aligned consistently. Keep the sample/fictional label visible beside both menu and visit details so sample content stays legible without feeling like a disclaimer wall.
Engineering constraint: keep the visit step static and truthful—use in-page menu/visit anchors and clearly sample address/hours; avoid dead order/contact controls or remote image dependencies.

content.text: QA edge case: on the phone viewport, tap Menu from the top, then Visit. Check that the anchor lands below any sticky header (so the section title is not hidden), and that a long dish name wraps without pushing its sample price off-screen. Those are the two likely decision blockers for someone browsing before walking over.

I’ve got the team’s direction: keep the first screen focused on food and the visit path, visibly mark sample details, and make in-page navigation work cleanly on a phone. I’m applying those constraints in one self-contained page now.

The draft is in place. The long mushroom taco uses a wrapping name with a separately aligned sample price, and the page’s anchor offsets account for the sticky navigation. I’m loading the saved file in the shared browser now to check layout and navigation at both sizes.

content.text:
Built the Taco Cometa site at [index.html](/workspace/outputs/index.html). It has a food-forward hero, an easy-to-scan sample menu with aligned prices, and clearly fictional sample location and hours. Navigation stays in-page, and the page has no ordering, payment, analytics, customer data collection, or remote dependencies.

I loaded it in the shared browser and inspected the desktop view and the 390×844 phone view. The long dish name has room to wrap while its price stays unbroken. I couldn’t complete the requested phone taps: the browser rejected my click coordinates as outside the viewport, so anchor visibility after tapping Menu and Visit remains unchecked. The sections do include offsets for the sticky header.

The shared Plan is updated, and the draft is ready for team review.

On phones, enlarge the “Sample menu · fictional prices” label and muted dish descriptions so they’re easy to read at a glance, while keeping the price alignment and airy layout. Please make this small targeted adjustment and update the Plan with it.

I’ll make the mobile-only type adjustment to the sample label and dish descriptions, leaving the menu grid, price column, and spacing intact. Then I’ll reload the shared browser at phone width and record the revision in the Plan.
